about: The book project as data: its dates, rounds, roles and decisions, from the editor's briefs of 30 October 2026 (briefs/2026-10-30/). The plan, team, decisions and book pages are built from this file. Items the editor decided are marked by=editor; everything else is a proposal for him to confirm or strike.
status: the plan is not signed yet, so no chapter is written. Round 0 (Friday 30 October): repositories up, the Leanpub book created, the build producing a PDF, the librarian's index started.
book_lead: A book about what was built on 29 October 2026: a ten-agent team, run by one person, that took a talk from nothing to on stage in one day, with the record to prove it. Two threads told as one story: **the workflow** (how the team was set up, briefed, scheduled, keyed, reviewed, held and released, and how to replicate it) and **the argument** (the talk itself: agents are the ultimate insider, and brakes are what let us go faster).
formats: Leanpub first (PDF and EPUB, set-your-own-price with a floor), then the Amazon KDP ebook, then a paperback with QR codes on the page pointing to the record. The manuscript in this repository, `manuscript/`, is the one source for all of them.

plan_lead: The talk was given at 19:00 on Thursday 29 October 2026. The work ended before it: the last change landed at 18:46 (release v0.1.209), and the editor's merge to main at 23:19 published it as v0.2.0 without changing it. The book is analysis written with hindsight, not a dump of the record: what was achieved, in what order, why it worked, what it cost, what went wrong, and what it means. Every chapter ends with where it came from.

team_lead: The roles proposed in the conductor's brief, on the talk team's machinery as it stands: a written mandate per member (`ROLE.md`, `policy.json`), the five-step wake, hourly slots, requests as files, session keys, holds, and a release on every merge. The conductor is staffed; the first batch (librarian, historian, security, researcher, storyteller, publisher) is proposed with its prompts in `team/conductor/ONBOARDING.md`; the rest follow when the plan is signed.
editor: Dinis Cruz is the editor: he decides, signs decisions, reads on paper, and is interviewed. Nobody else speaks for him.
blind: A second repository whose agents arrive knowing nothing but the talk's repository at commit `298be4e` (site v0.2.0) and write what they find. The one-way valve: the book repository reads the blind one; nothing flows the other way, or the blind repository stops being blind. No brief, chapter, decision or chat from here is ever copied into it.

decisions.ask: The price on Leanpub, with a floor
decisions.detail: The editor, in the conductor's session, 30 October 2026 about 10:40 UTC: "Ok, I reviewed the open questions and I agree with all the proposed answers, with the exception of the minimum Leanpub price which is going to be 0". A free minimum price ($0), at his word, against the team's proposal of $9.99; the suggested price $19.99, as proposed. His reasons, 30 October 2026, about 11:50 UTC: a reader he can email and send updates to is worth more than no reader; information should be shared, and someone who cannot afford the book should still have it; he prefers fewer paid sales and many more unpaid ones, for the halo effect, and because some readers come back to pay more or buy the next version. His correction, about 12:15 UTC: he does not need to email readers directly; he meant they are reachable, because every new version reaches them. And his main principle is accessibility: "I think you should be charged for content, but for people who can't afford it, they should still have access to it." Confirmed by the publisher from Leanpub's own page (30 October, about 15:00 UTC): "All readers get free updates, regardless of when they bought the book or how much they paid (including free)." Whether $0 readers also get the notice email is to be settled by a $0 test purchase.

decisions.ask: How a session is closed when another takes over its role
decisions.detail: Proposed by the conductor, 30 October 2026, at the editor's question "can you check if we have already a formal place to close the sessions?". There was none: WAKE.md's Finishing covers a member whose work is done, and admin/tools/pki-agent.README.md says to mark the previous session superseded. The editor's view, about 11:50 UTC: the conductor can write a handover on behalf of the previous session and sign it as itself, because often the old session cannot ("I'm running out of tokens on the other side and I want to keep a little bit"); it is "fundamentally a closing down of that session and then saying, okay, this is now the new one", and it must be announced, because agents that sign and send messages to one another "need to know that there's a new session ID"; the handovers should be mapped over time; it gives "a natural cadence for not having sessions with too long a context"; and "we need to just keep doing a lot of these until we get it right". Proposal, as a section "Handing over" in WAKE.md: (1) a handover closes the old session and opens the new one; the outgoing session writes it when it can, otherwise the conductor writes it on its behalf and signs it as itself (team/conductor/handovers/<id>.md); (2) the incoming session makes its key, marks the old session superseded with an until, adopts the handover in its first debrief and creates its own task; (3) the conductor records every handover in team/conductor/sessions-register.json and announces the new session id and key to every member by letter; (4) from the until, the old session pushes nothing as that role (a commit marked @<id>: from a superseded session is flagged to the editor); (5) the editor archives the old session in his own account. Options: A, as proposed; B, as proposed without (4); C, leave it to each handover. Decided A: the editor, in the conductor's session, 30 October 2026 about 13:00 UTC: "Yes that H1 plan is good". WAKE.md has its "Handing over" section.

decisions.ask: The team's hours while it waits on you
decisions.detail: Proposed by the conductor, 30 October 2026, 22:10 UTC: the editor's usage is a resource. Eleven members wake every two hours round the clock (Q2); the storyteller has had two idle wakes waiting on D6, and the next RC1 revision cannot start until D6 is signed. Options: A, keep every member's schedule as it is; B, narrow every member to 08:00 to 22:00 London (Q2 allows it); C, each member that is only waiting on the editor pauses its own task and the editor re-enables it when he signs; D, B and C together. Only the editor re-enables a task. Decided, the editor in the conductor's session, 30 October 2026 about 23:40 UTC: "the team hours should be roughly around the day, and then you don't have to do night"; and members "run like two or three times, maybe twice a day, unless they have active tasks. And so once they have active tasks, can they run more often? And then when they don't have active tasks, they can just run at a slower pace." WAKE.md has its Cadence section; the window and intervals are the conductor's reading of his words. Amended by the editor, 31 October 2026, about 01:20 UTC, in his RC1 review (briefs/2026-10-31__rc1-paper-review/batch-04-page-9.md): "we need to go back to increase the work throughout the night, because again, we don't have a lot of time and there's a lot of work to be done here ... we need to keep cracking on"; and "Don't limit the agents by 5 or 10 or 20 minutes ... it's okay for them to sometimes take 45 minutes ... They should never take more than an hour ... an agent that produces a lot of stuff in a session should clear his backlog". So: active members every two hours round the clock again, idle members twice a day; every wake uses its full time. At about 02:20 UTC on 31 October 2026, in the conductor's own session, at the editor's words "Yes, set them and fire them" (in answer to the conductor's offer to set every member's task to its round-the-clock schedule and fire each once), the conductor changed eight members' scheduled tasks and fired two. Today WAKE.md says a member changes only its own task. Options: A, yes, at the editor's word in the conductor's session each time, recorded on dev before the members' next wakes (WAKE.md says so); B, no, members change their own (the editor fires a task if it is urgent); C, only in an emergency, such as a hold.

decisions.ask: The book's structure and name, from the storyteller's study
decisions.detail: chapter-plan/study-name-and-structure.md, second pass (31 October 2026, 02:40 UTC). Structure: six parts, about 59,000 words: 1 the tour, 2 start with one agent, 3 grow the team, 4 the plumbing, 5 making the talk then containing it, 6 your turn; back matter for the logistics. Name: recommended N7 'Agents That Work Together: a guided tour of agentic workflows, and how to build yours'; alternative N8 'Brakes So We Can Go Faster: a guided tour of an agentic team at work, and how to build yours'; kept N2 and N1. Both go back to synthetic for a second round and to the researcher for an exact-title check before he signs. Signing it withdraws D6-1 to D6-4 (the storyteller's recommendation); D6-5 and D6-6 stand. The researcher's exact-title check (31 October 2026, about 04:55 UTC; comms/mail/mailroom/storyteller/researcher__002): neither N7 nor N8 is taken as a title; N7's words appear inside four 2026 Kindle subtitles. A check at the ISBN agency would close the gap. Footnotes: the team's build prints them at the end of each chapter; notes at the foot of the page need Leanpub's own PDF or another print engine (publishing/FOOTNOTES-AND-QR.md), his choice.

decisions.ask: Keep the book's content as JSON, with Markdown as a projection? (A7)
decisions.detail: The researcher's study, claims/json-book-study.md (31 October 2026): graphs.sgit.ai keeps Markdown as the source of truth with JSON as the machine surface (a book.json with chapters, words and a SHA-256 each, graphs anchored by byte offsets); this book already has that shape (Markdown prose; JSON plan and register). Three options in the study; the researcher recommends the third: Markdown stays the source, and the build gives every section and figure a stable id and emits a JSON graph. If he means JSON as the source, he should say so. books.sgraph.ai could not be read from the session (HTTP 502): the gap before he decides.

decisions.ask: The first ten pages of RC2, for the room, now
decisions.detail: Decided by the editor in the conductor's session, 31 October 2026, about 13:10 UTC (briefs/2026-10-31__in-session/01-the-first-ten-pages-and-the-gen-zx-series.md): "What about if you create a PDF or get the agents to create a PDF of like 10 pages of it, which I then review? And that should be almost like the first 10 pages of the book"; "let's get these first 10 pages ... this should be 10 pages that I should be able to send to everybody in that room, and they should be excited about it, and they should want to do it" (the room: the Vibathon Algarve 2026). The storyteller orders them, the publisher writes them as a sample outside Book.txt and builds the PDF (number and date on every page), the designer gives the look, the researcher traces every number, synthetic reads them as the room would, security reads them before he shares them. NS1 stays open; the sample may become RC2's opening if he signs it.

decisions.ask: This book as one of a Gen ZX Founders series, with its branding
decisions.detail: Floated by the editor, 31 October 2026, about 13:10 UTC (same brief): "maybe ... we can start to think of the Gen ZX founder as kind of a series of books and a series of materials. And this book is going to be one of that series", framed as "a book about you doing it. It's about you starting"; the cover and branding "compatible, or maybe reuse some of that ZX branding and reuse that Gen ZX founders tagline". Options: A, yes: series name and tagline on the cover and title page, ZX-compatible cover, the book's own title under it (NS1 still chooses that title); B, a lighter tie: the series named on the title page and the back cover only, this book's own cover; C, not now: publish this book on its own and wire up the series later. Conductor's recommendation: A, tried first on the ten-page sample (T10) and its cover sketch, so he can see it before signing; the Gen ZX Founders book's own team keeps its branding, and nothing is copied from its repository without his word. Decided by the editor, 31 October 2026, about 19:00 UTC (briefs/2026-10-31__in-session/02-g1-the-95-and-the-day-in-review.md): "yes, I think it should be a series with the on the title, on the cover page reference, and also in the explanation, maybe one of the first couple of pages that explains that, also explains the philosophy of it". So option A, and one of the first pages explains the series and its philosophy.
